name: Feasible Common-Scaling Interval
statement: Split logarithmic positive-row ratios as $z+t\mathbf1$ with $z$ in the zero-sum hyperplane. The feasible scales form $(\ell_C(z),u_C(z))$; finite endpoints are 1-Lipschitz in the sup norm and $u_C$ is concave. With $B_C=\{z:\ell_C(z)<u_C(z)\}$, one has $\mathcal A(C)\cong B_C\times\mathbb R^{1+d_-}$. If either endpoint is infinite, or there are no positive-row ratios, then $\mathcal A(C)\cong\mathbb R^{d_C}$.
proof: Upward and downward closure make each diagonal fiber an interval. Coordinatewise comparison gives the Lipschitz bounds, convexity of $\log V_C$ gives concavity of the upper endpoint, and an explicit logistic coordinate trivializes every finite interval over $B_C$.
